solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Baby model clutching a flower

indicators.note: clutching means holding something inside, so the model word wraps around the other pieces

parts.note: to model is to pose
a flower in crosswords is often a river, here the Po in Italy

explanation.surface: A fashion model poses with a baby holding a bloom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flower' is a thing that flows, a river, not a bloom; 'clutching' wraps the model word round A and the river.
explanation.definitionFit: A papoose is a Native American word for an infant, also a carrier for one.

clue.text: The old man, a fellow turning up in a hat

parts.note: pa is an informal word for father, one's old man

indicators.note: in a down entry turning up means the letters run upwards, reversed

parts.note: a man is a fellow

explanation.surface: Dad and a chap arrive wearing a hat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turning up' reverses A MAN to NAMA; 'the old man' is slang for father.
explanation.definitionFit: A Panama is a lightweight straw hat originally from Ecuador.

clue.text: Official policy to some extent silly, ultimately leading to row

parts.note: partly, in part

indicators.note: ultimately points to the last letter of the following word

parts.note: a line is a row

explanation.surface: A party's stance is partly foolish and ends up causing a quarrel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'row' reads as a quarrel but is a line.
explanation.definitionFit: A party line is the policy a political party officially holds.

clue.text: Insect beginning to go right down in bird

indicators.note: the first letter of the insect word drops all the way to the bottom of the down entry

parts.note: a louse is an insect

explanation.surface: A bug starts sliding down inside a bird.
explanation.walkthrough: L moves from the start of LOUSE to the end.
explanation.definitionFit: The ousel (ouzel) is an old name for the blackbird or the ring ouzel.

clue.text: A gift? Women tend to get excited

indicators.note: getting excited means stirred up, so the letters are mixed

explanation.surface: Asking whether women's tendency to excitement is a natural talent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to get excited' shuffles WOMEN TEND.
explanation.definitionFit: An endowment is a donation or a natural talent, both senses of a gift.

clue.text: Celeb, I'd go round making a bit of a noise?

indicators.note: to go round suggests the letters circling into a fresh order

explanation.surface: A celebrity spinning around causes a little commotion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'go round' is the anagram signal; the question mark marks the definition as playful, a unit rather than a noise itself.
explanation.definitionFit: A decibel is a unit measuring loudness, so one is a small measure of sound.

clue.text: Almost bashful making protest

indicators.note: almost means the last letter is left off

parts.note: demure means modest, shy

explanation.surface: A rather shy person lodges a complaint.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Almost' drops the last E of DEMURE.
explanation.definitionFit: To demur is to raise an objection.

clue.text: Suffering infant — doc could be someone to help by listening

indicators.note: suffering means in distress, so the letters are disturbed

explanation.surface: A sick baby; a doctor might be the one to hear the worries.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Suffering' rearranges INFANT DOC.
explanation.definitionFit: A confidant is a trusted person one shares secrets with, who hears them out.

clue.text: Bishop to emerge and thrive

parts.note: B is the chess abbreviation for bishop
to loom is to come into view

explanation.surface: A bishop comes forward and prospers.
explanation.definitionFit: To bloom is to flourish, as in a person in good health.

clue.text: Showing great desire, soldiers shine

parts.note: lust is a strong desire
RE, the Royal Engineers, a British Army corps

explanation.surface: Eager troops polish their gear.
explanation.walkthrough: RE is the Royal Engineers, a corps of the British Army.
explanation.definitionFit: Lustre is a gleam or sheen on a surface.

clue.text: Opening trap, moving front bit back

definitions.note: the answer is the plural of a single nostril opening; the clue's singular is loose

indicators.note: the first letter of the trap word is shifted to its end

parts.note: a snare is a trap

explanation.surface: Instructions for opening a trap by shifting its front piece.
explanation.walkthrough: 'moving front bit back' takes the S from the front of SNARE to the end.
explanation.definitionFit: Nares is the anatomical term for nostrils, the openings of the nose.

clue.text: Act put on by servants in overseas territories?

indicators.note: put on by means the first piece is placed before (on top of) the second in the across entry

parts.note: to act is to do
minions are servants

explanation.surface: A show performed by the household staff.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put on' looks like staging a show but means placed in front of; the question mark flags the historical, Empire sense.
explanation.definitionFit: Dominions were self-governing countries of the British Empire, far from Britain.

clue.text: Shrub won't necessarily 7

definitions.meaning: a hawthorn bush, whose blossom comes in May
7 down is BLOOM; something that might bloom but need not, read as two words

explanation.walkthrough: The second definition splits the answer into two words: 'may' (perhaps) and 'flower' (bloom, the answer to 7).
explanation.definitionFit: Hawthorn is called mayflower after the month its blossom opens; also 'might blossom' as a phrase.

clue.text: Is lake reported in this foreign city?

indicators.note: reported means the words are spoken and heard rather than written

parts.note: a mere is a lake, so this says 'is mere'

explanation.surface: A traveller asks whether a lake is said to lie in some city abroad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reported' turns IS MERE into a sound-alike of the Turkish city.
explanation.definitionFit: Izmir is a large port city in western Turkey, so a city abroad for the setter.

clue.text: Team with charm — where might they arrive unnoticed?

parts.note: a side is a team in sport
to entrance is to charm

explanation.surface: A charming team wonders where to slip in quietly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'charm' is a verb here, giving ENTRANCE, which then reads as a noun, a way in.
explanation.definitionFit: A side door or way in lets people come and go away from the main front.

clue.text: Trevor Howard helping Celia Johnson in film? Something to surprise us

definitions.text: Trevor Howard helping Celia Johnson in film?
definitions.meaning: in the British film Brief Encounter (1945) Howard's doctor removes grit from Johnson's eye, freeing it

explanation.walkthrough: Brief Encounter is a classic 1945 British romance; the lovers meet when he takes a speck out of her eye at a railway station.
explanation.definitionFit: A revelation is something that opens your eyes to the truth.

clue.text: See 13
Is stander around demonstrating this?

indicators.note: around suggests the letters being moved about

explanation.surface: Is someone hanging about showing a lack of punctuality?
explanation.walkthrough: 'around' is the anagram signal; the whole clue also describes the answer, since one who stands around is late doing things.
explanation.definitionFit: Lateness or slowness: someone loitering shows a failure to be prompt.

clue.text: Centre in which US jazz fan shows sparkle

indicators.note: in which means the following pieces go inside the centre word

parts.note: the core is the centre
cat is old slang for a jazz enthusiast

explanation.surface: A US jazz club where a fan dazzles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in which' puts the pieces inside the centre word; cat is old jazz-age slang for a fan.
explanation.definitionFit: To coruscate is to flash or glitter, give off sparkles.

clue.text: Yeoman shoos away loud bird

indicators.note: shoos away means driving something off, so a letter is removed

parts.note: a Beefeater is a Yeoman Warder at the Tower of London
f (forte) is the musical sign for loud

explanation.surface: A Tower guard chases off a noisy bird.
explanation.walkthrough: Beefeaters are the ceremonial guards at the Tower of London; 'shoos away' drops F.
explanation.definitionFit: The bee-eater is a brightly coloured bird that catches flying insects such as bees.

clue.text: Something edible old rodent's brought back

indicators.note: brought back says the letters are read in the reverse direction

parts.note: a rat is a rodent; the 's is 'is', a link

explanation.surface: An old rat brings home some food.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brought back' reverses ORAT.
explanation.definitionFit: Taro is a tropical plant whose starchy root is cooked and eaten.

clue.text: Naughty nudes getting quiet ridicule

indicators.note: naughty means misbehaving, so the letters are disarranged

parts.note: p (piano) is the musical sign for quiet

explanation.surface: Racy nude pictures attract hushed mockery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Naughty' turns NUDES into SENDU.
explanation.definitionFit: A send-up is a parody or a mocking imitation.

clue.text: King once setting up some stupid laws ostentatiously

indicators.note: setting up says the hidden letters are read backwards
some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A former monarch who established some foolish laws with show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'setting up' reverses the run in a down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: Oswald was a 7th-century king of Northumbria, later a saint.

clue.text: Is Parisian going to work in bar?

parts.note: est is French for 'is'
op (opus) is a work

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a Parisian is off to work in a pub.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bar' is the legal verb, not a pub.
explanation.definitionFit: In law to estop is to prevent or preclude someone from asserting something.

clue.text: Bone — a small piece I swallowed going the wrong way

indicators.note: going the wrong way means reading the letters backwards, upwards here
swallowed means taken inside

parts.note: a bit is a small piece

explanation.surface: A bone fragment someone swallowed went down the wrong way.
explanation.walkthrough: I goes inside A BIT to make AIBIT, then 'going the wrong way' reverses it.
explanation.definitionFit: The tibia is the shinbone of the leg.

clue.text: Executives holding investigation — they may be off on a trip

definitions.text: they may be off on a trip

indicators.note: holding means containing, so one word sits inside the other

parts.note: suits is slang for executives
a case is an investigation

explanation.surface: Bosses running an inquiry, possibly before heading off on travels.
explanation.walkthrough: 'holding' puts the investigation word inside the executives; 'suits' is slang for office bosses.
explanation.definitionFit: Luggage goes on journeys, so cases are things that may set off travelling.

clue.text: Thus manage to get drunk

parts.note: so means thus
to use is to manage or handle

explanation.surface: Somebody contrives to become intoxicated.
explanation.definitionFit: To souse is to drench, and soused is slang for intoxicated.

clue.text: Commander left in charge is a pain

parts.note: CO is commanding officer

explanation.surface: An officer left in command is a nuisance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a pain' looks like a nuisance but is a literal ache.
explanation.definitionFit: Colic is severe abdominal pain, common in babies.

clue.text: Certificate to be getting bitten, it seems!

indicators.note: getting signals being placed inside, being bitten by false teeth

parts.note: being bitten implies teeth doing the biting, here a set of false teeth

explanation.surface: A document that seems to come with a nasty bite.
explanation.walkthrough: 'getting' puts BE inside the false teeth that 'bitten' implies; 'it seems!' admits the teeth are only suggested.
explanation.definitionFit: A debenture is a bond or certificate acknowledging a loan to a company.

clue.text: Beast left to be housed by priest

indicators.note: housed by means the first piece goes inside the second

parts.note: a lama is a Tibetan Buddhist priest

explanation.surface: An animal left in the care of a priest.
explanation.walkthrough: L goes inside LAMA.
explanation.definitionFit: A llama is a South American pack animal related to the camel.

clue.text: Publicists will need to publicise — that is plain

parts.note: PR stands for public relations, the publicists' trade
to air an idea is to publicise it
i.e. is the Latin abbreviation for 'that is'

explanation.surface: Spin doctors must spread the word; that much is obvious.
explanation.walkthrough: 'plain' seems to mean obvious but is a grassland.
explanation.definitionFit: A prairie is a wide flat grassland, a plain of North America.

clue.text: Come after triumph

definitions.meaning: to follow on, as an heir does a monarch

explanation.definitionFit: To succeed is both to follow someone into a role and to achieve success.
